result.title: Odds-Structured Distributional Regression for Interpretable Time-to-Event Prediction
result.summary: Time-to-event prediction is fundamentally challenged by partial observability and aleatoric uncertainty. In clinical medicine, for instance, the timing of disease progression or acute readmission is contingent on highly dynamic and largely latent health trajectories. Rather than forcing a deterministic point forecast, distributional regression offers a principled means to address this complexity by predicting a probability distribution over time. However, explaining these distributional predictions presents a key obstacle: raw distribution parameters output by the model are abstract mathematical quantities that do not align well with domain concepts. To gain interpretability, we propose a novel paradigm where output parameters are designed to be additive in log-odds---a widely established measure in clinical risk modeling. Our approach, called ODDS-DR, moves beyond technical convenience to deliver clear domain alignment as well as the layer-wise computational structure required for robust, time-dependent feature attribution. Validated across two real-world clinical cohorts, our framework matches state-of-the-art predictive performance while resolving distributional outputs into interpretable risk markers across flexible prognostic horizons.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ODDS-DR，把事件时间预测的分布输出参数设计成 log-odds 可加形式，在保持分布回归预测性能的同时，支持随预测时间窗变化的逐层特征归因，并在两个临床队列上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 log-odds 可加分解与逐层、时间依赖的归因结构，可能为 LVR 中跨推理步的贡献分配与 latent 状态可解释性提供概念对照，可供核查；与视觉多模态推理本身无直接联系。
